necb_rules.json.note: The umbrella carries only article_coverage: what the pipeline itself determines. Article numbers and titles were transcribed from NECB 2020 Division B Section 8.4 and cross-checked against the building-codes MCP; the status/how/code fields are the pipeline's self-declaration and have no external source to re-fetch. The code pointers are checked by tests/test_coverage_code_refs.py, the article text by the packaged coverage/articles_8_4.json. The 20 h floor under 8.4.1.2.(4)'s cooling unmet-hours allowance moved from a code literal in compliance.py into this file (unmet_cooling.minimum_allowance_h) on 2026-09-08, multi-edition plan Stage 5; the value is unchanged and the source is unchanged.

tables/space_types.json.note: The 308 records are the legacy MERGED standards_data (deep merge along NECB2011<-2015<-2017<-2020, later keys win) — what legacy actually runs; the per-vintage files are partial. Checked against the oracle at REF while writing this block: 286 of the 308 records are byte-identical to NECB2020/data/space_types.json and the remaining 22 differ only by keys inherited from the earlier vintages. Units are IP as in legacy.

tables/schedules.json.note: NECB2017 and NECB2020 ship no schedules table, so the merge resolves to NECB2015's: checked against the oracle at REF while writing this block, all 240 shipped records are byte-identical to NECB2015/data/schedules.json. Set A was cell-verified against printed Table A-8.4.3.2.(1)-A via the MCP (see loads_rules.json).

tables/daylighting_controls_4_2_1_6.json.note: Re-read 2026-07-30 from the extraction canmet-energy/hbix#88 corrected. The two daylight-control columns are keyed by the 105 NECB space-function catalog names rather than by table row, and each catalog name was mapped to a row by hand and checked by comparing the catalog's lighting_per_area against the row's LPD (102 of 102 agree). The 2025 edition's own 4.2.1.6 payload was compared at generation time — 0 differing cells of 909 — which is why the two editions ship byte-identical files; that is a finding, not a dependency.

coverage/articles_8_4.json.note: THE CACHE IS THE RETAINED ARTIFACT, so source_sha256 == result_sha256 and no separate payload is stored: this document is the canonicalised output of one get_section call per Section 8.4 article, with page furniture stripped and each article parsed into a sentence/clause tree under strict sanity checks (an article that fails any check keeps parse_ok:false and its raw text). What is NOT retained is the raw per-article JSON-RPC result; re-fetching reproduces the cache, not a byte-identical payload set. Written by the Ruby fetcher at c7b0bf7 (2026-08-20), which the current python/scripts/fetch_necb_8_4_text.py ports with cache-schema parity; the Ruby original retired with the gems under D-84 and is reachable at that commit.
